description: Vector embeddings and knowledge graph: Build ChromaDB collections for semantic search over well-type manuals, SOPs, maintenance reports, and context notes. Create NetworkX graph representing well-area-team-user relationships and equipment hierarchy. Generate sentence-transformer embeddings for all text documents. This feature is independent of FEAT-001 but uses its SQLite data.
steps: Write backend/scripts/build_embeddings.py: Initialize ChromaDB persistent client at data/chroma/. Create 4 collections: 'manuals' (well-type manuals: T200.md, T350.md), 'sops' (spill-response-sop.md, regulatory-compliance-sop.md), 'reports' (all maintenance-reports/*.md files), 'context' (context notes from context_notes table). Use sentence-transformers model 'all-MiniLM-L6-v2' (384 dimensions) for embeddings. Chunk manuals and SOPs by section (split on '## ' headers), store full markdown reports as single documents. For each document, add metadata: {source_file, doc_type, asset_id (for reports/context), section_name (for manuals/sops), created_at}. Generate unique IDs as {collection}_{asset_id}_{index}.

Implement chunking strategy in build_embeddings.py: For T200.md and T350.md, split into sections (e.g., '## 3. Production temperature rule', '## 9. Engineering limits'). Store section text with metadata {well_type_code, section_number, section_title}. For SOPs, split by protocol (e.g., 'SR-01', 'RC-02') using regex to detect protocol IDs. For maintenance reports, keep full report as one chunk (reports are typically 200-400 words, fit in embedding model context). For context notes, combine note_type, text, and author into single string.

Write backend/scripts/build_knowledge_graph.py: Create NetworkX directed graph with node types: Well, Area, Team, User, Equipment. Add edges: Well→Area (belongs_to), Area→Team (managed_by), Team→User (has_member), User→Team (leads, for team leads), Well→User (in_charge), Well→Equipment (has_component), Equipment→Equipment (connected_to, for wellhead→pump_jack→rod_string→downhole_pump→flowline sequence). Query SQLite to get nodes and relationships from wells, areas, teams, users, equipment tables. Store node attributes (e.g., Well: {asset_id, name, well_type, lat, lon, status}, User: {user_id, name, role}). Export to data/graph/knowledge_graph.json using networkx.node_link_data().

Add graph traversal utilities in build_knowledge_graph.py: Implement helper functions get_well_hierarchy(asset_id) → {area, team, team_lead, in_charge_user, equipment_list}, get_area_wells(area_id) → [asset_ids], get_user_wells(user_id) → [asset_ids]. Store these as precomputed indexes in knowledge_graph.json metadata section for fast lookup during agent queries.
acceptance_criteria: ChromaDB collections created at data/chroma/ with 4 collections: manuals (2 documents with ~30 chunks), sops (2 documents with ~20 chunks), reports (~1500 documents), context (~600 documents)
Each chunk has embeddings (384-dim vectors) generated by sentence-transformers 'all-MiniLM-L6-v2'
Metadata includes source_file, doc_type, asset_id (where applicable), section_name (for manuals/sops), created_at
NetworkX graph saved to data/graph/knowledge_graph.json with ~2500 nodes (200 wells + 1000 equipment + 4 areas + 4 teams + 15 users) and ~5000 edges
Graph has 5 node types: Well, Area, Team, User, Equipment with correct attributes from SQLite
Precomputed indexes in knowledge_graph.json: well_hierarchy (200 entries), area_wells (4 entries), user_wells (~15 entries)
verification: Verify ChromaDB: python -c "import chromadb; client = chromadb.PersistentClient(path='data/chroma'); print(client.list_collections()); print(client.get_collection('reports').count())" — expect 4 collections, reports count ~1500

Verify embeddings: python -c "import chromadb; client = chromadb.PersistentClient(path='data/chroma'); coll = client.get_collection('manuals'); res = coll.query(query_texts=['production temperature rule'], n_results=1); print(res['metadatas'][0])" — expect metadata with well_type_code='T200' or 'T350'

Verify graph structure: python -c "import json; g = json.load(open('data/graph/knowledge_graph.json')); nodes = g['nodes']; print(f'Nodes: {len(nodes)}'); print(f'Node types: {set(n["type"] for n in nodes)}')" — expect ~2500 nodes with types: Well, Area, Team, User, Equipment

Verify graph relationships: python -c "import json; g = json.load(open('data/graph/knowledge_graph.json')); edges = g['links']; print(f'Edges: {len(edges)}'); print(f'Edge types: {set(e["relation"] for e in edges)}')" — expect ~5000 edges with relations: belongs_to, managed_by, has_member, leads, in_charge, has_component, connected_to
